comments.body:
Approved refinement applied after auditing current parsers and maintained-project prior art. RP-05 now requires one side-effect-free stdlib argparse factory per command grammar; execution and generation use the same factory. Generated package-help/overview bytes remain committed and runtime-authoritative so help stays pre-operation and no-extras. The CLI reference consumes those artifacts; curated prose/examples remain editorial and may not define unchecked usage/option tables.

S2 was decomposed because the prior hand-written-help scope was too large for one reviewable leaf:
- `tremendous-comely-blesbok` (S2a): parser/route foundation and shadow parity.
- `fancy-felonious-ant` (S2b): core command parser migration.
- `groundable-expectable-grackle` (S2c): advanced/nested parser migration.
- `ammonitoid-senile-nighthawk` (S2d): deterministic artifact generation and pre-operation help cutover.

S2b/S2c depend on S2a; S2d depends on both. Existing S3/S4 still depend on the S2 container, so no execution/capability cutover can precede the complete parser/help contract. S1, S3, S5, S6, epic file impact, and verification plans were updated. Research is durable on `rubellite-secondary-cub`; no production/tracked file changed and no blocked plan review was forced.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
Rebar's CLI facade on current main is 714 lines and reconstructs command identity and policy through 19 overlapping frozensets, an intercept ladder, package-help filenames, a regex-based reference generator, and repeated test censuses. The existing CLI reference is generated, but its syntax authority is not: it embeds 54 hand-maintained help resources plus a curated intercept table, so parser/help drift can pass while the census remains complete.

Twenty-one intercept-only commands lack safe canonical help. `rebar help <command>` reports them unknown, while handler-owned `--help` is inconsistent and can execute work. The maintainer approved normalizing every visible command and approved deriving syntax/options from the same parser definitions used by execution.

## Approved Architecture
Create one stdlib-only immutable lazy route registry. A route records canonical identity, spellings/visibility, lazy handler and parser-factory references, a bounded invocation-adapter kind, generated package-help key, mount/init policy, confirmation/output policy, and possible semantic capabilities. The registry is a routing table, not a plugin system, DI container, or middleware framework.

Every command grammar is built by a side-effect-free stdlib `argparse` factory. Runtime handlers and build-time generation call that same factory. Existing argparse builders are extracted; imperative parsers migrate with accepted/rejected argv, `--` handling, diagnostics, streams, and exit codes pinned by behavioral tests. A narrow shared ArgumentParser subclass/formatter may preserve Rebar diagnostics; no docs-only parser, source-regex grammar, Click dependency, or second parser is introduced.

Generation resolves all parser factories at build/check time using fixed `prog`, width, and formatter policy, then commits package-help and overview bytes. Runtime overview/help, aliases, malformed global syntax, and unknown-command output read only those bytes before RP-04 operation snapshot, config materialization, mount, handler resolution, or optional imports. The lexical top-level selector identifies only the spelling and first-token help/unknown forms; nested argv remains selected-handler-owned.

A separate semantic capability registry maps capabilities to packaging extras and missing postures: `error`, `unavailable`, `abstain`, or intentional `fallback`. Routes advertise possibilities only; checks occur after the selected mode/backend is known, and domain components retain degraded result shapes.

## Compatibility Contracts
Exact aliases reuse canonical grammar/help. `bridge-fsck`, `bridge-probe`, and `jira-onboard` compose canonical argument-definition helpers with alias-specific `prog`/replacement prose; `jira-onboard` keeps its historical spelling. Hidden `bridge-status` is explicitly helpable but undiscoverable. `purge-bridge` remains unknown.

Help/unknown paths never compose an operation or mount. Execution retains central best-effort mount, strict init, confirmation/global-output behavior, legacy JSON shapes, tokens after `--`, and established streams/exit codes. Accepted grammar changes are limited to the separately approved safe-help normalization unless a ticket names another intentional delta. `rebar-mcp` remains a separate entry point.

## Migration and Rollback
Use expand/contract by command family. Add the registry/parser contract and derived compatibility exports; migrate each handler and its runtime parser together; generate authoritative artifacts only after the complete parser/route census passes; then move execution, capabilities, docs/distribution consumers, and finally remove compatibility authorities. No shipped phase may contain a docs-only grammar runtime ignores.

During expansion, rollback selects derived compatibility exports and reverts a parser family with its generated artifacts. After contraction, code revert restores the old router. Ticket, event, bridge, and binding formats do not change.

## Delivery Order
1. Record the architecture decision and prior-art constraints.
2. Establish the parser/registry foundation; migrate core and advanced parser families in parallel; generate canonical package help only after both complete.
3. Migrate lazy execution and semantic capability boundaries.
4. Derive reference/distribution checks from registries and generated parser artifacts.
5. Retire duplicate authorities and complete cutover.

## Testing
Use unit tests for pure registry/parser validation; command-family production-path parity tests for accepted/rejected argv and errors; real subprocess tests for exact committed bytes, streams, exit codes, aliases, and absence of operation/config/mount/handler effects; a clean no-extras wheel for every help form; and a full-extra lane for lazy-reference resolution. Generator `--check` must prove parser-rendered artifacts and `docs/cli-reference.md` are byte-current.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Every command's runtime parsing and generated syntax/options come from one side-effect-free argparse factory; no docs-only/manual syntax authority remains.
- [ ] Every visible canonical command appears once in the grouped overview and both top-level help forms return byte-current generated package data before operation/config/store/handler boundaries.
- [ ] Exact, compatibility, hidden, and retired spellings exhibit the approved behavior, including historical `jira-onboard` and unknown `purge-bridge`.
- [ ] Lazy execution preserves mount/init, argv, confirmation, stream, exit-code, and legacy-output contracts except the explicit help normalization.
- [ ] Selected optional modes/backends preserve approved capability postures without eager optional imports.
- [ ] CLI-reference generation, coverage, lean-wheel checks, and full-extra resolution enumerate registries/parser artifacts rather than source regexes or manual command censuses.
- [ ] Duplicate authorities are removed after shadow parity; quality gates pass and no stored-data migration occurs.
- [ ] ADR 0099 and living architecture record the parser, route, capability, migration, compatibility, and rollback boundaries.
